signals.label: Yahoo preseason ADP
signals.note: Preseason ADP is fixed once the season starts; undrafted players count as replacement level.

signals.label: FantasyPros consensus (ECR)
signals.note: FantasyPros has not published rest-of-season rankings yet; its page serves the final draft consensus.

market.curve: 100 x (e^-(position-1)/40 - e^-(R-1)/40), R = rostered active players

assumptions: Trades take effect from 2026-10-24: 1 day for the partner to accept plus the 2-day commissioner reject window. Earlier games count for the original teams.
Every other team keeps its deterministic forecast; any matchup with the trade partner is recomputed with both new rosters.

Each team keeps at most 14 active players. The side taking two players clears a spot with its best legal drop among its all cheapest options (Can't Cut players excluded when the list is captured), or an IL move for an O/INJ player when an IL slot is free (IL eligibility unverified).

An open spot is scored as left open. A free-agent fill is shown separately: it uses one acquisition in the effective week, relies on free-agent status at capture, never uses waiver players, and counts only partly in ranking.
Trades themselves use no acquisitions. Keeper value, manager preferences, injury return dates and pending trades are not modelled.

Category-win changes are deterministic projections, not probabilities. Market value and your competitive benefit are kept apart. Market value is how other managers are likely to see players: the mean of Yahoo preseason ADP and FantasyPros consensus rankings, each re-ranked among Yahoo's players and put on one auction-like curve; on a side with two players the second counts at half (the side that gets the best player is the one managers see as winning); any player a side must cut counts against that side. Paying the partner a market premium is allowed and ranked by what it buys; a package where the partner loses more than 10% by market value is never shown. Model value (z-scores over replacement) is shown only as an asset-sacrifice risk. None of this predicts acceptance.
